title: Chunk Atlas — Real-Time Fluency: Response Tokens & Active Listenership

questions.question: You're listening to someone talk and want to signal you're following along, without taking the turn yourself. Which chunk fits best?
questions.explanation:
✓ Correct — "Uh-huh." is a Continuers — Keeping the Channel Open chunk: used while listening to signal you're following along, without taking the turn.
Example: ""So first we tried the old server..." "Uh-huh." "...and that didn't fix it either.""
Similar chunks:
- Right.
- Sure.
- Mm-hm.

✗ "Was it?" belongs to More Newsmarkers (Showing Interest) — used as a light, quick way to show interest in what was just said, not this context.
Similar chunks:
- Oh?
- Has it?
- Really?

✗ "No way." belongs to Assessments — Surprise & Strong Agreement — used to react with surprise, or to strongly back up a point someone just made, not this context.
Similar chunks:
- You're kidding.
- Absolutely.
- Exactly.

✗ "Poor you." belongs to More Sympathy Tokens (Bad News) — used as a stronger sympathetic reaction when someone shares bad news, not this context.
Similar chunks:
- Nightmare.
- That's rotten.
- Ouch.

questions.question: You're listening to someone talk and want to signal you're following along, without taking the turn yourself. Which chunk fits best?
questions.explanation:
✗ "Spot on." belongs to More Surprise & Agreement Tokens — used as a stronger or more colorful reaction to surprising news or a strong point, not this context.
Similar chunks:
- Get out.
- Precisely.
- You're joking.

✗ "That's great news." belongs to Reacting When They're Happy or Boasting — used to match a colleague's excitement when they're happy or a bit proud about something, not this context.
Similar chunks:
- Look at you!
- You must be pleased.
- Get in!

✓ Correct — "Mm-hm." is a Continuers — Keeping the Channel Open chunk: used while listening to signal you're following along, without taking the turn.
Example: ""...and then the client called back at five." "Mm-hm." "...saying they wanted a full refund.""
Similar chunks:
- Right.
- And then?
- Okay.

✗ "That sounds stressful." belongs to Reacting When They're Worried, Explaining, or Apologizing — used to respond appropriately when someone is anxious, explaining themselves, or apologizing, not this context.
Similar chunks:
- It's fine, really.
- These things happen.
- I get why.
